main_text.l: tum populum rogent: Atque hic quidem merito illis
sensus est, fuit quippe domus tua aliquot ab hinc retro
seculis Themidis sacrarium, Vosque ex illa inter princi-
pes Iustitiæ Sacerdotes, de quibus verè dixerim quicquid
Græcia mendax audet in historiis de suo Solone,
chylo, Demetrio Phalereo, aliis, quibus Rempublicam
suam optimis ornatam LEGIBVS, atque constitutam
Atheniensis imputat populus: Sed vt & tibi, VIR
ILLVSTRISSIME, eos in ædes tuas admittendi sit ani-
mus, cùm nullo possim meo merito, precè à te expe-
to, & enixè rogo: ita faxit Deus Opt. Max. sic voueo,
sic spero, vt, qui sanctissimum tuum parentem, qui ma-
iores tuos, viros supra omnem laudem, iam virtutibus
æquasti, cumulatis honoribus longe superes. Vale
A. D. VIII. kal. Ianuarias anni Dionysiani MDXXXV.

page.notes: The first word "tum" is a fragment from the previous page. The printed reading of the salutation is "ILLVSRISSIME" (no T), kept as printed. The date is printed in reversed-C numerals (CIↃ IↃCXXXV) and is given here as MDXXXV (1535). The word "ILLVSRISSIME" and the date are read from a small, slightly blurred print. The Greek phrase "Græcia" is in roman, and "LEGIBVS" is in small capitals, which are copied as capitals.
